name: Cross-country skiing
energy: Very high aerobic demand (world-class VO2max, maximal oxygen uptake, above 80 ml/kg/min for men, about 70 for women) using the whole body, with hard surges on climbs and in sprint heats.
summary: Cross-country skiing is whole-body endurance where poling power and leg drive both matter, and the lower back is the most injured area. The plan uses heavy upper-body pulling and leg strength to improve poling economy, plus back, shoulder and lateral hip work.

evidence.claim: Nine weeks of heavy upper-body strength training improved double-poling economy and time to exhaustion in cross-country skiers.
evidence.source: Osteras, Helgerud & Hoff 2002, European Journal of Applied Physiology

evidence.claim: World-class skiers train about 860 h a year, with about 6% as strength training; skiing and roller skiing make up 68% of endurance time.
evidence.source: Walther et al. 2023, Frontiers in Physiology

evidence.claim: Cross-country skiing has the lowest injury rate of the World Cup ski disciplines, 6.3 time-loss injuries per 100 athletes a season.
evidence.source: Florenes et al. 2012, Scandinavian Journal of Medicine and Science in Sports

variants.name: Classic
variants.desc: Double poling and diagonal stride: lats, triceps and trunk flexion do much of the work.
variants.note: Your plan adds straight-arm pulldowns and triceps work to match the double-pole stroke.

add.note: Hinge at the hips like a pole stroke

variants.name: Skate
variants.desc: A lateral push off an edged ski: more single-leg and lateral hip power.
variants.note: Your plan adds lateral bounds and lateral lunges for the skating push.

add.note: Push out and slightly forward, stick 1 s

variants.name: UK roller skier
variants.desc: Most specific training is on roller skis on tarmac, where falls hurt more and snow time is short.
variants.note: Your plan adds wrist and forearm work for falls and poling. Always ski with a helmet and gloves.

off.name: Heavy upper pull and poling
off.focus: Max strength for the poling stroke

slots.note: Fast and hard, like a sprint pole stroke

off.name: Heavy legs
off.focus: Leg strength for kick and climbs

off.name: Long easy endurance
off.work: 60-120 min roller ski, run, bike or hike
off.why: World-class skiers do about 90% of their endurance time at low intensity.

off.name: Double-pole intervals
off.work: 5-6 x 4 min on SkiErg or roller skis, double pole only
off.why: Upper-body endurance that transfers to the poling stroke.

pre.name: Ski walking and bounding uphill
pre.why: The classic dryland session for diagonal stride power and VO2max.

pre.name: Sprint heats
pre.work: 4-6 x 3 min on roller skis or SkiErg
pre.intensity: Race pace for a sprint heat
pre.why: Sprint heats last about 3 min, so this trains repeat heats.

tests.name: Max pull-ups
tests.how: Dead hang start, chin over bar, no kipping.
tests.note: Women about half. Bands are a coaching guide.

tests.name: Countermovement jump
tests.how: Hands on hips, jump app or mat, best of 3.

tests.name: SkiErg 1000 m
tests.how: Double pole only, damper 5-7, full effort, after a warm-up.
tests.note: Compare with yourself; same damper every time.

tests.name: Back extension hold
tests.how: Hips on the edge of a bench, body straight, time until you drop.
tests.note: Tracks lower back endurance. Compare with yourself.

tests.name: Lateral bound for distance
tests.how: Bound sideways off one leg, stick the landing, best of 3 each side.

week: Lift after easy sessions or 6+ hours after hard ones.
Never lift heavy the day before intervals or a race.
Split upper and lower days, like elite skiers pair uphill and double-pole days.
Race weekends: last gym session 3-4 days before.
primer: 2 x 3 med ball slams for sprint days

lines: Cut gym sets by about half; keep loads heavy.
Arrive at altitude or snow early if you can; first days on snow feel hard.

rules: Roller ski with a helmet and gloves, on quiet roads, and only where you can stop.
Ramp off-season running slowly; overuse injuries peak in the off-season.
Lower back work every week, all year.
No heavy lifting the day before intervals or racing.
